newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel sees support at $25.00.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel sees support at $25.00.

text.p: Singapore diesel prices continued to enjoy high levels for early April cargoes but traders said on Friday the steeply backwardated market would see levels falling to its $25.00 support for late April cargoes.

They noted that Taiwan only managed to sell its end-April lifting cargo at $25.16 a barrel, free-on-board, even though the Singapore market continued to be traded at over $28.00 for end-March/early April and at over $27.00 for first half April cargoes.
Taiwan's 225,000-250,000-barrel cargo was sold to the same Singapore trader who had already bought 2.32 million barrels of gas oil over the past two weeks.

The same trader on Friday bought another 150,000 barrels for March 29-April 4 lifting at $28.40 fob from a European major, and another similar sized cargo at $27.40 for April 6-10 lifting fob, from a Dutch trader.
Another cargo was heard sold to the trader at $27.20 for early April lifting fob.

The buyer was expected to remain in the market into next week, after which prices were expected to slide amid concerns that around 500,000-700,000 tonnes of arbitrage cargoes were expected to arrive to Asia from the West and MidEast in April.
Some traders believe that the total volume might be up to 1.0 million tonnes and many offers would be seen from late March.
But other traders noted that if the Singapore trader decided to stop its buying spree and prices fell, the arbitrage might close again.
Traders said the bulk of diesel that the Singapore trader has acquired would go to Indonesia, while some would go into floating storage off China.

Traders also noted that stocks in Hong Kong are very low as China has absorbed large volumes in small barge lots. China also has the potential to buy more during the current shutdown season which will last until May.
This could provide some support to the market, which they said would not slide below $25.00 which has been the bottom for about two months.
Traders also noted that with gas oil well supported, and jet fuel entering its low demand season, the physical regrade would remain at negative levels for some time.
Jet fuel for April 9-13 lifting was offered at $26.80, while another parcel for April 6-10 lifting was offered at $27.00, below the levels traded on gas oil.
